---
title: "Renderings (R)"
format:
  html:
    code-tools: true
filters:
  - panzoom
---

R cells with `renderings: [light, dark]`, which draw one plot for each color
mode. The page shows the one for its mode (the toggle in the navbar), and so
does the viewer. Each one is worth opening in light and dark mode.

The transparent plots use the `ragg_png` device, since the base R png device
tints light text drawn on a transparent background.

The plots are drawn with this helper:

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "wave()"

#' Draw a sine wave with shading to zero.
#'
#' @param k Frequency multiplier; the curve completes 2 * k cycles on 0 to 4 * pi.
#' @param ink Color for the axes, labels, and title.
#' @param paper Plot background color, or NULL to keep the device background.
#' @param col Color for the curve and its shaded area.
wave <- function(k = 1, ink = "black", paper = NULL, col = "#3B7DB8") {
  if (!is.null(paper)) {
    par(bg = paper)
  }
  par(fg = ink, col.axis = ink, col.lab = ink, col.main = ink)
  x <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 400)
  plot(
    x,
    sin(k * x),
    type = "n",
    main = paste("Wave", k),
    xlab = "x",
    ylab = "sin(kx)"
  )
  polygon(
    c(x, rev(x)),
    c(sin(k * x), rep(0, length(x))),
    col = adjustcolor(col, 0.35),
    border = NA
  )
  lines(x, sin(k * x), lwd = 2, col = col)
}
```

## Light and dark renderings {expect-open="panzoom"}

A cell with two plots: black ink on white for light mode, and light gray ink on
near-black for dark mode. It opens in panzoom with the plot for the current
color mode.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| renderings: [light, dark]
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in blue on a background matching the page"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 3: y = sin(3x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(k = 3, paper = "white")
wave(k = 3, ink = "gray85", paper = "#1E1E1E", col = "#7FB8E6")
```

## Transparent renderings {expect-open="panzoom"}

A cell with two plots on a transparent background: black ink for light mode and
light gray ink for dark mode. It opens in panzoom with the plot for the current
color mode.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: ragg_png
#| dev.args: !expr list(bg = "transparent")
#| renderings: [light, dark]
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in blue with axes in the text color"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 4: y = sin(4x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(k = 4)
wave(k = 4, ink = "gray85")
```

## Gallery with light and dark renderings {expect-open="panzoom" expect-steps="true"}

Two cells with `renderings: [light, dark]`, joined by `group: renderings`. The
gallery steps through the two plots for the current mode.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: renderings
#| dev: ragg_png
#| dev.args: !expr list(bg = "transparent")
#| renderings: [light, dark]
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in blue with axes in the text color"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 5: y = sin(5x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(k = 5)
wave(k = 5, ink = "gray85")
```

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: renderings
#| dev: ragg_png
#| dev.args: !expr list(bg = "transparent")
#| renderings: [light, dark]
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in blue with axes in the text color"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 6: y = sin(6x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(k = 6)
wave(k = 6, ink = "gray85")
```

## Renderings in the other order {expect-open="panzoom"}

A cell with `renderings: [dark, light]`: the first plot, with light gray ink, is
for dark mode, and the second, with black ink, for light mode. It opens in
panzoom with the plot for the current color mode, as with the default order.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: ragg_png
#| dev.args: !expr list(bg = "transparent")
#| renderings: [dark, light]
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in blue with axes in the text color"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 2: y = sin(2x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(k = 2, ink = "gray85")
wave(k = 2)
```
